findings.title: Preserve committed-write status after successful publication
findings.evidence: The new warning branch tests Workspace::wrote(), whose contract is events the remote does not have yet (crates/beadroll-store/src/workspace.rs:120-127), not whether this command committed. cli::finish publishes before calling note_unpublished (cli.rs:360-366); a successful exchange calls note_sync and then set_wrote(false) (beadroll-sync/src/synchronise.rs:193-195). note_sync deliberately ignores metadata-save errors (workspace.rs:233-240), leaving the old count available. Demonstrated on the pinned tip in a scratch repository and local bare remote: initialize and create one issue (two journal lines), set that segment's published count to the string 2-i128::MAX, verify list --json succeeds with unpublished=i128::MAX, then run comments add KEY "exactly once" --json without --offline and with BEAD_FAILPOINTS=atomic-write:meta.json=errno(ENOSPC). The comment is durably appended and published, but the final count exits 1, emits no stdout and returns {"error":{"code":"IO",...}} instead of the successful result and warning. /tmp/beadroll-review-publish-3elp89ar/result.json records the actual command result, journal growth from 2 to 3, remote_contains_comment=true, and the one persisted comment. This violates R1 and can induce a duplicate retry of a non-idempotent write. Preserve whether the command committed independently of the mutable unpublished-write flag, including callers which publish within the command, and add a regression for successful publication followed by failed count bookkeeping. The existing AF01 test always appends --offline and therefore does not exercise this path.

acceptance.evidence: Reviewed both note_unpublished callers (cli::finish and commands::init), Outcome::count_warning delivery, stderr JSON rendering, read-only error handling, and the AF01 object/array/silent/human/init cases. The offline crossing regression correctly starts at a valid i128::MAX count, makes one durable write, retains stdout, and preserves subsequent read-only IO errors. However, the demonstrated online publication/metadata-save failure in post_publish_count_loses_committed_state still converts a committed, remotely published comment into failure. Controller baseline-stress passed, but its AF01 test does not cover this supported path.

commands/show.rs:104-107 reads priority through IntegerField, whose Display is numeric (core/op.rs:81-84) while to_value retains booleans (op.rs:41-46). The list path already uses this numeric Display. commands/format_policy.rs:33-80 covers true and false in human list and show and verifies detail JSON remains boolean. The rendering change is local; generic repr/repr_str diagnostic quoting is unchanged. The controller baseline passed these CLI tests.

Inspected the complete accumulated source/test diff b5d5543da780c7ed71210407fbe709130ab5e4f3..719b46d8a5d253342b1748d661efe14d9d591794, including Int parsing/arithmetic/float bounds and every changed consumer, ASCII numeric inputs, conflict JSON presentation, export collision increments, segment rotation, metadata count arithmetic, key admission/renaming/minting, and ownership application/replay. Numbered-key admission remains below 4300 digits and duplicate renaming increments text beyond i128. Native exhausted claims refuse before issue mutation; replay removes exhausted takeover supersession, preserves awaiting across retries, and projection extension either shares application or requests replay for takeovers. Numeric-limit/legacy-fixture, projection, rotation, pending-count, parser/settings and golden tests substantiate these boundaries. No format-1 writer encoding, core I/O boundary, dependency edge or general diagnostic quoting changed. Historical review reports were not used as independent review inputs, as required by this assignment.

AF01 and AF02 ledger entries name their focused regressions in docs/FINDINGS.md:34-35; README, CHANGELOG, GUARANTEES and REVIEWING describe the committed-result warning policy and boolean display policy. Inspected every explicitly supplied validation log: controller baseline-stress receipt 00017 reports 1205/1205 tests, 14 infra tests and 2/2 stress tests passed; receipts 00018 through 00024 record exit 0 for formatting, workspace lint, fuzz formatting/lint, both dependency checks and support build at this fingerprint/content hash. Dependency-check warnings are only unused license allowances. These execution facts do not cure the R1 behavior defect. Source/index remained unchanged and HEAD remains the pinned tip.
